## What Will LCCC Charge for Tuition?

$4,613 In-State Tuition & Fees$10,913 Out-of-State Tuition & Fees

For the most recent year on record, in-state undergraduate tuition and fees at Laramie County Community College ran **$4,613** annually. Out-of-state undergraduates were charged **$10,913**. The difference reflects the in-state residency discount.

Required fees account for came to **$1,463** in-state and **$1,463** out-of-state; the remainder is straight tuition.

|  | In-State | Out-of-State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tuition | $3,150 | $9,450 |
| Fees | $1,463 | $1,463 |
| **Total** | **$4,613** | **$10,913** |

This tuition and fees total reflects one year of study and leave out [room and board](https://www.collegefactual.com/colleges/laramie-county-community-college/paying-for-college/room-and-board/).

Keep in mind that many students qualify for [financial aid and scholarships](https://www.collegefactual.com/colleges/laramie-county-community-college/paying-for-college/financial-aid/) that reduce the amount they actually pay. The totals here are the list price.

## What Will LCCC Charge for Tuition?

$4,613 In-State Tuition & Fees$10,913 Out-of-State Tuition & Fees

For the most recent year on record, in-state undergraduate tuition and fees at Laramie County Community College ran **$4,613** annually. Out-of-state undergraduates were charged **$10,913**. The difference reflects the in-state residency discount.

Required fees account for came to **$1,463** in-state and **$1,463** out-of-state; the remainder is straight tuition.

| Tuition | $3,150 | $9,450 |
| Fees | $1,463 | $1,463 |
| **Total** | **$4,613** | **$10,913** |

This tuition and fees total reflects one year of study and leave out [room and board](https://www.collegefactual.com/colleges/laramie-county-community-college/paying-for-college/room-and-board/).

## About

Laramie County Community College is a higher education institution located in [Laramie County, WY](https://datausa.io/profile/geo/05000US56021). In 2024, the most popular Associates Degree concentrations at Laramie County Community College were [Registered Nursing](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/513801) (70 degrees awarded), [General Business](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/520101) (39 degrees), and [General Health & Wellness](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/510001) (30 degrees).

In 2024, 844 degrees were awarded across all undergraduate and graduate programs at Laramie County Community College. 57.2% of these degrees were awarded to women, and 42.8% awarded men. The most common race/ethnicity group of degree recipients was white (536 degrees), 3.7 times more than then the next closest race/ethnicity group, hispanic or latino (145 degrees).

The median undergraduate tuition at Laramie County Community College is $3,150, which is $−5,010 less than the national average for [Associates Colleges](https://datausa.io/profile/university/ASC) ($8,160).

## About

Laramie County Community College is a higher education institution located in [Laramie County, WY](https://datausa.io/profile/geo/05000US56021). In 2024, the most popular Associates Degree concentrations at Laramie County Community College were [Registered Nursing](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/513801) (70 degrees awarded), [General Business](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/520101) (39 degrees), and [General Health & Wellness](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/510001) (30 degrees).

In 2024, 844 degrees were awarded across all undergraduate and graduate programs at Laramie County Community College. 57.2% of these degrees were awarded to women, and 42.8% awarded men. The most common race/ethnicity group of degree recipients was white (536 degrees), 3.7 times more than then the next closest race/ethnicity group, hispanic or latino (145 degrees).

The median undergraduate tuition at Laramie County Community College is $3,150, which is $−5,010 less than the national average for [Associates Colleges](https://datausa.io/profile/university/ASC) ($8,160).

# University of Wyoming Tuition & Financial Aid

University of Wyoming's tuition is $8,245 for in-state and $24,865 for out-of-state students. Compared with the national average cost of in-state tuition of $12,436, University of Wyoming is cheaper. For students coming from out of state, the tuition is cheaper than the national average cost of out-of-state tuition of $29,815.

These figures include both tuition and fees, also referred to as the [sticker price](https://www.usnews.com/education/best-colleges/paying-for-college/articles/paying-for-college-infographic). Fees differ by institution and may fund library services, student gym facilities, student centers, technology resources and campus health centers.

As you’re comparing costs of different institutions, also consider the total cost and the net price. The total cost is the sticker price, plus the cost of food and housing, books and supplies, and transportation and personal expenses. At University of Wyoming, the total cost is $26,433 for in-state students and $42,843 for out-of-state students. The net price is the average cost of the university after aid and scholarship funds are discounted from the total cost, which come in on average at $19,099 for in-state students and $37,297 for out-of-state students receiving need-based aid.

## Financial Aid Statistics for University of Wyoming

Financial aid refers to funding that students can use to pay for college and is generally [awarded based on need or merit](https://www.usnews.com/education/best-colleges/paying-for-college/articles/an-ultimate-guide-to-understanding-college-financial-aid).

Need-based aid is determined by your or your family’s demonstrated ability to pay for college, as calculated by the Free Application for Federal Student Aid, known as the FAFSA. The average need-based scholarship or grant awarded to first-year students at University of Wyoming was $7,571. Additionally, 49% of first-year students received need-based financial aid in fall 2023.

Need-based self-help aid includes federal loans and work-study. The average need-based self-help aid awarded to first-year students was $3,071.

Merit-based aid, also called non-need-based aid, is awarded for a specific talent or academic achievement. The average non-need-based scholarship or grant awarded to first-year students at University of Wyoming – excluding any athletic scholarships, if applicable – was $4,945.

## Student Loan Debt for University of Wyoming

How much student loan debt you accumulate can affect your financial life long after college ends. Ideally, your total [student loan debt](https://loans.usnews.com/how-student-loans-affect-your-credit) should fall below your anticipated starting salary once you graduate.

At University of Wyoming, the median federal loan debt among borrowers who completed their undergraduate degree is $18,000. The median monthly federal loan payment (if it were repaid over 10 years at 5.05% interest) for student federal loan borrowers who graduated is $191.

Additionally, 8% of graduating students at University of Wyoming took out private loans. Students with private loans had an average of $35,907 in private loan debt at graduation.

# University of Wyoming Tuition & Financial Aid

University of Wyoming's tuition is $8,245 for in-state and $24,865 for out-of-state students. Compared with the national average cost of in-state tuition of $12,436, University of Wyoming is cheaper. For students coming from out of state, the tuition is cheaper than the national average cost of out-of-state tuition of $29,815.

These figures include both tuition and fees, also referred to as the [sticker price](https://www.usnews.com/education/best-colleges/paying-for-college/articles/paying-for-college-infographic). Fees differ by institution and may fund library services, student gym facilities, student centers, technology resources and campus health centers.

As you’re comparing costs of different institutions, also consider the total cost and the net price. The total cost is the sticker price, plus the cost of food and housing, books and supplies, and transportation and personal expenses. At University of Wyoming, the total cost is $26,433 for in-state students and $42,843 for out-of-state students. The net price is the average cost of the university after aid and scholarship funds are discounted from the total cost, which come in on average at $19,099 for in-state students and $37,297 for out-of-state students receiving need-based aid.

### COA COMPONENTS

**Residency**

*   **Wyoming Resident**- an **undergraduate student** who will/has graduate(d) from a high school in the state of Wyoming will be considered a Wyoming resident student. A **graduate student** who has established residency for tuition purposes, as determined by the Office of the Registrar, will be considered a Wyoming resident student. The Master of Health Services Administration program uses the Wyoming Resident rate for Wyoming residents, UW Alumni, and affiliated organizations.
*   **Non-Resident & International** - a student who is not a resident of the state of Wyoming will be considered a non-resident or international student.
*   **Alumni** - a student who graduated with a degree from the University of Wyoming will qualify for the Alumni tuition benefit. A student (undergraduate or graduate) who is an out-of-state resident, with either parent having graduated with a degree from the University of Wyoming, will qualify for the Children of Alumni tuition benefit.

**Tuition and Fees**

*   Standard online undergraduate programs are based on a **block tuition rate** for students enrolled in 12-18 credit hours per semester. If enrolled in more or less than the block rate, tuition will adjust accordingly.
*   Online undergraduate and graduate programs are based on a **non-block tuition rate**, dependent upon residency status, and enrollment requirements that are determined by the length of program.
*   **Mandatory fees** include distance delivery, student services, and advising. They are applied dependent on enrollment status. Some programs may incur additional fees, which are included on the appropriate COA grid. Distance delivery fees are $14 per credit hour, student services fees are $35 per credit hour, and advising fees are $10 per credit hour (undergraduate only).Note: All undergraduate first-time and transfer students will incur a $150 Onboarding Fee during their first semester of enrollment; this is not included in our Fees estimate above but should be considered for students within those populations.
*   See our [Tuition and Fees](https://www.uwyo.edu/fsbo/student-financial-services/tuition-and-fees.html) page for more information.

Living Expenses

*   A housing allowance for students who live **off-campus** is based on an average of student survey and publicly reported county housing data for one bedroom living arrangements, including utility expenses.
*   A housing allowance for students who live **at home** with parents is based on a percentage of the off-campus costs.
*   A **food**allowance that provides the average of student survey data and publicly reported county grocery data for for students who live**off-campus** or **at home**.

**Books, Course Materials, Supplies, and Equipment**

*   An estimate based on student survey data and national data.

**Other Expenses**

*   **Transportation**- an estimate based on an average of transportation expenses by our peer institutions.

### COA COMPONENTS

**Residency**

*   **Wyoming Resident**- an **undergraduate student** who will/has graduate(d) from a high school in the state of Wyoming will be considered a Wyoming resident student. A **graduate student** who has established residency for tuition purposes, as determined by the Office of the Registrar, will be considered a Wyoming resident student. The Master of Health Services Administration program uses the Wyoming Resident rate for Wyoming residents, UW Alumni, and affiliated organizations.
*   **Non-Resident & International** - a student who is not a resident of the state of Wyoming will be considered a non-resident or international student.
*   **Alumni** - a student who graduated with a degree from the University of Wyoming will qualify for the Alumni tuition benefit. A student (undergraduate or graduate) who is an out-of-state resident, with either parent having graduated with a degree from the University of Wyoming, will qualify for the Children of Alumni tuition benefit.

**Tuition and Fees**

*   Standard online undergraduate programs are based on a **block tuition rate** for students enrolled in 12-18 credit hours per semester. If enrolled in more or less than the block rate, tuition will adjust accordingly.
*   Online undergraduate and graduate programs are based on a **non-block tuition rate**, dependent upon residency status, and enrollment requirements that are determined by the length of program.
*   **Mandatory fees** include distance delivery, student services, and advising. They are applied dependent on enrollment status. Some programs may incur additional fees, which are included on the appropriate COA grid. Distance delivery fees are $14 per credit hour, student services fees are $35 per credit hour, and advising fees are $10 per credit hour (undergraduate only).Note: All undergraduate first-time and transfer students will incur a $150 Onboarding Fee during their first semester of enrollment; this is not included in our Fees estimate above but should be considered for students within those populations.
*   See our [Tuition and Fees](https://www.uwyo.edu/fsbo/student-financial-services/tuition-and-fees.html) page for more information.

Living Expenses

*   A housing allowance for students who live **off-campus** is based on an average of student survey and publicly reported county housing data for one bedroom living arrangements, including utility expenses.
*   A housing allowance for students who live **at home** with parents is based on a percentage of the off-campus costs.
*   A **food**allowance that provides the average of student survey data and publicly reported county grocery data for for students who live**off-campus** or **at home**.

**Books, Course Materials, Supplies, and Equipment**

*   An estimate based on student survey data and national data.

**Other Expenses**

*   **Transportation**- an estimate based on an average of transportation expenses by our peer institutions.
*   **Miscellaneous Personal Expenses** - an estimated based on student survey data and may include laundry and dry cleaning, personal hygiene items, personal grooming, necessary clothing, shoes, and entertainment.

## How Much Might UW Charge for Tuition Plus Fees?

$7,768 In-State Tuition & Fees$24,178 Out-of-State Tuition & Fees

In the latest reported year, in-state undergraduate tuition and fees at University of Wyoming were **$7,768** for the year. Out-of-state undergraduates paid **$24,178**. That gap is the in-state discount at this school.

The fees portion of those totals added up to **$2,578** in-state and **$2,578** out-of-state; the remainder is straight tuition.

|  | In-State | Out-of-State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tuition | $5,190 | $21,600 |
| Fees | $2,578 | $2,578 |
| **Total** | **$7,768** | **$24,178** |

This tuition and fees total reflects one year of study and leave out [room and board](https://www.collegefactual.com/colleges/university-of-wyoming/paying-for-college/room-and-board/).

Bear in mind that many undergraduates get [financial aid and scholarships](https://www.collegefactual.com/colleges/university-of-wyoming/paying-for-college/financial-aid/) that reduce the amount they actually pay. The totals here are the list price.

Wyoming's tuition & fees has increased from $12,770 (2015) to $24,178 (2025), and the rate of tuition increase is 89.33% over the past 10 years. The graduate school tuition & fees has raised from $13,796 (year 2015) to $21,822 (year 2025).

The 2025 tuition & fees have risen more than 5% this year (2025) at University of Wyoming.

Wyoming's tuition increase rate is higher than the Wyoming's average increase rate of 6.48%. Compare to all colleges in United States, it's increase rate is higher than the average increase rate of 10.99%.
